rationale: The request presents workflow-level friction across dashboard submission, email approval, timeout recovery, duplicate prevention, and ownership, so Fructal Cap Design applies. The no-modification boundary caps the requested replacement flow at Redesign. The response defines a coherent end-to-end state model, retry/idempotency behavior, ownership transitions, handoff, recovery, source of truth, preserved approval constraints, and a proportionate verification plan without writing to the fixture. It correctly distinguishes the requester-reported workflow from the directly observed minimal fixture and explicitly avoids claiming validation. Material implementation choices remain open, including whether ownership is queue-based or assigned to a named approver and the exact escalation ownership.
